audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-focused specifications: EVM opcode behavior (environment, block instructions), precompiled contracts (secp256r1, alt_bn128), state trie operations, transaction validation (EIP-3607), receipt formats (EIP-658), difficulty calculation (Arrow Glacier), and peripheral protocols (EIP-1571 mining stratum, EIP-1102 account access).

out_of_scope: Mining pool protocol internals (EIP-1571 is peripheral)

el_attack_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, attempt address collision exploits (EIP-3607), resource exhaustion via precompile spam, craft invalid EVM inputs
Propagate blocks with invalid difficulty (Arrow Glacier), blocks containing transactions from contract addresses, blocks with corrupted state roots
Submit invalid curve points to BN128/secp256r1 precompiles, attempt gas exhaustion via underpriced operations, exploit return data bounds

cl_attack_vectors.threat: Manipulate block context values within consensus-allowed bounds to influence on-chain randomness or time-dependent logic

misclassified_entities.reason: Executing smart contract is an internal EL component, not an external entity. It executes within the EVM and is part of the system under audit. The actual external entity is the user/DApp that submitted the transaction triggering contract execution.
Calling contract is internal to the EVM. The external entity is the transaction submitter whose input eventually reaches the precompile via contract execution.
ZK verifier contract is an internal EVM component. The external entity is the proof submitter providing the ZK proof data.
Historical block storage is internal state. Not an external entity.
Key provider is an internal abstraction for trie key inputs. The actual external entity is the transaction that provides the address/storage key.
Transaction sender is already captured by the more general 'User via JSON-RPC' entity. Receipt generation is an internal process.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users and DApps submit transactions and simulation requests via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. All input is potentially malicious: malformed transactions, transactions from contract addresses (EIP-3607 attack vector), crafted calldata targeting precompiles with invalid curve points or out-of-bounds parameters. No authentication required for public RPC endpoints.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes propagate blocks and transactions over unauthenticated P2P network. Peers may send blocks with invalid difficulty calculations, blocks containing transactions from contract-address senders, or blocks with corrupted receipt/state roots. Eclipse attacks possible.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Validator) via Consensus
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block header fields (COINBASE, TIMESTAMP, PREVRANDAO, difficulty)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators set block context values consumed by EVM opcodes. While constrained by consensus rules (timestamp monotonicity, difficulty formula, PREVRANDAO from randao mix), validators have limited influence over these values within allowed bounds. Authenticated via consensus mechanism but content must be validated against protocol rules.

trusted_external_entities.name: WebAuthn/FIDO2 Device via Transaction Calldata
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Signature data from external hardware security devices (Apple Secure Enclave, Android Keystore, FIDO2) enters the EVM as calldata to the secp256r1 precompile. Despite originating from secure hardware, the data traverses untrusted channels (browser, network, smart contract) before reaching the precompile. All cryptographic validity checks (curve membership, bounds, signature verification) must be performed. Signatures may be malleable (both (r,s) and (r,n-s) valid).

trusted_external_entities.name: ZK Proof Submitter via Transaction Calldata
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: alt_bn128 precompiles (add, mul, pairing check) calldata
trusted_external_entities.rationale: ZK proof data enters the EVM as calldata targeting BN128 precompiles. Input may contain points not on the curve, coordinates exceeding field modulus, wrong subgroup order, or input lengths not divisible by expected sizes. All validation must be performed before computation. Gas is consumed regardless of validity (DoS protection).

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Browser Provider (window.ethereum)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Web applications request account access via the browser provider API. DApps are untrusted third-party code running in the browser. They may attempt repeated requests to fatigue users, spoof origin information, or manipulate consent dialogs. User approval is the trust boundary gate.

trusted_external_entities.name: Mining Client via Stratum Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Mining clients connect via unauthenticated TCP to pool servers. They may send malformed JSON messages, invalid hex formatting, unauthorized worker tokens, stale job submissions, or attempt session hijacking via forged session IDs. Worker credential validation is required at each step.

trusted_external_entities.name: Mining Pool Server via Stratum Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Pool servers push mining configuration and jobs to clients. A malicious or compromised pool could distribute invalid work, manipulate target difficulty, redirect hash power, or provide incorrect epoch/extranonce parameters. No TLS or authentication is mandated by the protocol.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature recovery, nonce verification, EIP-3607 sender code hash check (CodeHash must equal EMPTYCODEHASH), gas limit validation, balance sufficiency. Transactions from addresses with deployed code MUST be rejected.
Simulation requests MAY bypass EIP-3607 sender code check. Input parameters must still be validated for format correctness. Resource consumption must be bounded by gas limits.

Full block validation required: difficulty must match expected value (Arrow Glacier formula with 10,700,000 offset), all transactions must pass EIP-3607 sender code check, receipt status codes must be consistent with execution outcomes, state root must match after applying all transactions.
Same transaction validation as JSON-RPC submission. Transactions from peers are untrusted and require full validation including EIP-3607 checks.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block header fields consumed by EVM opcodes (COINBASE, TIMESTAMP, NUMBER, PREVRANDAO, GASLIMIT, CHAINID)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block context values must be validated against consensus rules: TIMESTAMP must be monotonically increasing, difficulty must match Arrow Glacier formula, PREVRANDAO sourced from beacon chain randao mix, GASLIMIT within adjustment bounds. EVM opcodes read these values as trusted after block validation passes.

Input must be exactly 160 bytes. Signature bounds: 0 < r < n, 0 < s < n. Public key bounds: 0 <= qx < p, 0 <= qy < p. Point must satisfy curve equation and not be point at infinity. Gas (6900) consumed regardless of input validity. Returns empty (not revert) on failure. Applications must handle signature malleability.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: alt_bn128 precompiles (add at 0x06, mul at 0x07, pairing at 0x08)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All coordinates must be less than field modulus. Points must be on BN128 curve (y^2 = x^3 + 3). For pairing: input length must be divisible by 192, points must have correct subgroup order. Gas costs: add=150, mul=6000, pairing=34000*pairs+45000. OutOfGasError signals failure for both gas exhaustion and invalid input (indistinguishable to caller).

Provider must display approval dialog isolated from DApp manipulation. Origin must be faithfully displayed to user. Repeated requests after rejection should be rate-limited. Response must contain at least one valid account address if approved.

All JSON messages must be validated: proper JSON format with LF termination, correct message type (request/response/notification), lowercase hex with no 0x prefix, valid worker tokens for submissions, active job IDs. Error counting with maxerrors threshold for connection termination. Session resumption must validate session ID against cache.

Mining configuration and job data from pool must be validated: epoch number consistency, target difficulty reasonableness, extranonce within 6-byte limit, header hash format validity. No TLS mandated, so MITM is possible. Miners should verify work independently when possible.
